rationale: Evidence from iteration 7 (sensor_size 0.016, kp 3.0, kd 0.8, ki 0, base_speed 1.0), now the best raced design at 633.93 (up from 600.47). Oval held at 20 of 20 (progress 0.998, steering_oscillation 0.30). S-bend finishes rose from 14 to 15 of 20, with 5 off-track ends and mean progress 0.96. Slalom progress rose from 0.215 to 0.371, the largest slalom gain so far, though it still has 0 of 20 completions and 1.15 line-loss events per run. Gain changes (kp 3.5, ki 0.05) did not move slalom, while the sensing footprint did, so sensing is the slalom lever. The Evaluator's rule applies: slalom progress is above 0.25 with the oval still at 20 of 20, so keep geometry.sensor_size at 0.016 and test a sensor spacing refinement. Change (one variable from the best design): sensor x positions from -0.04, -0.02, 0, 0.02, 0.04 to -0.03, -0.015, 0, 0.015, 0.03. The span narrows from 0.08 m to 0.06 m, which tests whether a tighter array keeps the outer sensors on the tape through the slalom's alternating bends. Weights, kp 3.0, kd 0.8, ki 0, base_speed 1.0, sensor_size 0.016 and line_loss last_direction are all unchanged. Expected result (a hypothesis, not a measurement): slalom progress rises further toward 0.4 or more and slalom line-loss events fall, with the oval still at 20 of 20 and s-bend finishes at 14 or more. Risks: a narrower array may reduce the steering signal at large offsets and let the robot leave the track on the slalom's sharpest bends, and the s-bend could lose finishes. Reading the race: (a) if slalom progress rises and the oval and s-bend hold, spacing is helping and the next step is base_speed 1.2 or a slalom-specific test; (b) if s-bend finishes fall below 14 or the oval drops, return to the iteration 7 spacing (0.02 steps) and keep sensor_size 0.016; (c) if slalom stays flat near 0.37, the bend geometry or base_speed is the limit, so test base_speed 0.8 to 0.9 next. Measurements wanted: completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation and control_effort on all three tracks.
